FIRST FIRE.LOCAL IMPACT   /   INDIA

Built in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh

From a Moon cabin to an Indian oxygen ward

The question FIRST FIRE asks about the Moon is a question Indian hospitals have faced in real fires: what happens to a fire when the air holds more oxygen than usual? The physics is the same. Only the gravity changes.

See oxygen-enriched air in the fire lab →

The problem on Earth

Hospital fires in oxygen-rich wards

122 deaths in 29 major hospital fires in about 20 months.

That was the count of a media compilation across India from August 2020, during the COVID-19 surge (Quartz, from Scroll.in).

ICUs are the most exposed rooms.

Electrical faults started most fires in a study of 33 major hospital fires. Doctors quoted in the same report noted that an "oxygen-rich environment provides fuel to the fire" in intensive care (Quartz).

Fires in COVID wards cost lives across states.

Fires killed 13 COVID-19 patients in Virar, Maharashtra (AP, April 2021) and 18 in an ICU in Bharuch, Gujarat (Al Jazeera, May 2021). An inquiry into the Ahmednagar ward fire, which killed 11, found missing safety equipment (The National, November 2021).

The link to the Moon

One physics, two worlds

Oxygen limitMore oxygen means a smaller safety margin.

Every material has an oxygen limit. Raise the oxygen in the air, as near a patient's oxygen supply, and more materials pass their limit, exactly as in a 34% Moon cabin.

 Air flowFans can feed a flame or starve it.

FLINT shows that cutting the air flow helps some materials and hurts others. That is a warning against treating "switch the fans off" as a universal response.

 Try itCompare 21% and 25% oxygen.

Set Earth gravity and normal pressure in the fire lab, then raise the oxygen and watch the margins shrink. The lab marks these settings as a model extrapolation.

 Materials firstThe fix is the material.

In the Moon rover, flooding and venting are poor fire responses; choosing materials that cannot burn in the air they sit in is the reliable answer. Bedding, curtains and tubing in oxygen wards face the same choice.

FIRST FIRE models thin solid materials in spacecraft conditions. It does not model hospital bedding or cotton, and it is not a fire-safety standard. Hospitals should follow the national guidelines on fire and life safety in healthcare facilities and the Health Ministry and NDMA advisory on preventing hospital fires.

India in space

Gaganyaan and a station of our own

India is preparing to fly its own astronauts in Gaganyaan and plans a space station. Every material in a sealed crew cabin faces the question FIRST FIRE answers: will it keep burning in that air, at that gravity? The tools here are open, free and work offline, so Indian students and engineers can use them without an account.
